title: Order Header
description: Header-level structure shared by every order and sub-order: identity, lineage, target, and status. An order's positions (line items) are defined separately - see order-position.schema.json. This schema describes the SHAPE order/sub-order instances must have; actual live instances are runtime data (in the WMS/OMS), not tracked in this repo - see structure/fields.yaml for how one order_type restricts/extends this shape.

order_type.description: References the order_type this header belongs to.

parent_order_id.description: Empty/absent for a top-level order. Set for a sub-order created by a split_rule, or spawned by a completion_rule's spawn_order/reallocate_remainder action.

source_split_rule.description: References the split_rule.id that created this sub-order, if any.

target.description: The MOVEMENT TARGET: the destination this specific order/sub-order's executing system must physically reach - the next reachable hop, not necessarily the final business destination. Decided once at order/sub-order creation time (by the runtime OMS/WMS, typically via a routing/connectivity-graph lookup), not re-resolved dynamically here. A sub-order's target may differ from its parent's and from its own order_target - e.g. an AutoStore sub-order's target is the cell's own EXIT work_center because that system can only move goods that far, not all the way to the order's real destination. See docs/entity-glossary.md and order_target below.

order_target.description: The ORDER TARGET: the immutable business destination for this order line, set once on the top-level order and inherited UNCHANGED by every descendant sub-order, no matter how many times it is split or re-split (split_rule.target_override and completion_rule.reallocate_remainder only ever change 'target', never this field). An order/sub-order is only truly fulfilled once its confirmed quantity is reached AND target == order_target - if a system can only reach an intermediate point, the quantity condition is met but this target condition is not, which is what completion_rule's 'when.target_gap' watches for.

status.description: References a statuses[].id from this order_type's structure/status.yaml.

target.description: A destination reference - a Topology-as-Code entity (door/work_center/activity_area). Used both as 'target' (this order/sub-order's own next reachable hop) and 'order_target' (the immutable final business destination) - see the two properties above for how they differ.

type.description: The Topology-as-Code entity kind this target references.

id.description: The Topology-as-Code id of the door/work_center/activity_area.
